title: 1951 AHSME Problem 44
statement: If \(\dfrac{xy}{x+y}=a,\) \(\dfrac{xz}{x+z}=b,\) and \(\dfrac{yz}{y+z}=c,\) where \(a,\) \(b,\) \(c\) are other than zero, then \(x\) equals:

solutions.text:
Inverting gives \[ \begin{gathered} \frac1x+\frac1y=\frac1a,\\ \frac1x+\frac1z=\frac1b,\\ \frac1y+\frac1z=\frac1c. \end{gathered} \] Adding the first two and subtracting the third yields \[ \begin{aligned} \frac2x &=\frac1a+\frac1b-\frac1c\\ &=\frac{ac+bc-ab}{abc}. \end{aligned} \] Hence \(x=\dfrac{2abc}{ac+bc-ab}.\)

Thus, the correct answer is E.
hints: Invert all three given equations to make them linear in \(\frac{1}{x},\frac{1}{y},\frac{1}{z}\)
